correctness.rationale: For fixed integer N≥2, the full Cauchy/Poisson harmonic-measure derivation proves the published stationary density without assuming ergodicity. The binomial ratio gives K_N=N(N²−1)/3 as the exact first parameter coefficient. A change of variables gives the exact gap tail. Dominated convergence proves the two off-critical moment laws; an explicit three-interval integral split gives the critical logarithm and an O(β^(-1/2)) uniform remainder for bounded crossover coordinate s. Exact algebra and numerical checks in check.py match all stated constants. Boundary α=N uniqueness and finite-time dynamics are not claimed.

value.rationale: The loss of a smooth invariant state at α=N is a natural statistical bifurcation. The whole family of stationary observables (1−x)^q has a sharp threshold at q=1/2; below it the concentrating core controls the response, and above it rare macroscopic excursions dominate. The uniform crossover H(s), exact constants and degree calibration produce a meaningful natural complete classification useful for approximating stationary measures and interpreting non-differentiable response near the endpoint. It is more than a renamed integral or an isolated numerically evaluated parameter slice.
